plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a mutual consequential-damages exclusion with direct-damage clarifications, and an Excluded Claims definition covering confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud and IP. Check 21.4 for savings language and 18.2 (insurance does not limit liability). Likely compliant.

Vendor IP indemnity in 20.1 and misconduct/law/data indemnity in 20.2; Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 appears narrow with carve-outs. Procedure in 20.4 and infringement remedies in 20.5 (cross-referenced by 9.3). Confirm indemnities sit outside the cap via 21.3.

Section 12.3 expressly preserves Customer's freedom to develop, buy, or compete and disclaims exclusivity/non-compete. Check for conflict with the exclusivity language in sec-2.2 (first 2.2), which is an exclusivity rather than non-compete issue; do not double-flag.

The first Section 2.2 makes Vendor Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the term — a direct hit and likely deviation, notwithstanding the contrary disclaimer in 12.3 and the no-commitment language in 2.1. Note the internal conflict and duplicate 2.2 numbering.

The first Section 7.2 requires Customer to give Vendor terms no less favourable than its best terms to any other technology supplier — an MFN running against us, contrary to the rule's direction and to 12.3's disclaimer. Likely deviation.

Section 12.4 binds Customer for eighteen months post-termination, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, bars engagement as well as solicitation, and has no general-advertising carve-out; 12.3 contains a contrary general-recruitment carve-out. Likely deviation.

Section 9 provides only termination for cause, insolvency, and specific Vendor failures; no Customer right to terminate for convenience on notice appears (note there is no 9.4 in the outline). Check 8.2 non-renewal and 27.3 force-majeure exit before concluding the rule is missing.

Section 8.2 auto-renews Order Forms for twelve months on a 180-day non-renewal notice — likely too long a window; 8.3 caps uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice, which supports the pricing limb. Focus any redline on the notice period only.
New York law with New York County courts and no foreign arbitration; CISG excluded and an escalation step in 28.3 that does not bar urgent relief. Likely compliant.

24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor; 24.4 blocks Vendor termination or repricing on our change of control; 13.3 allows transfer of licence rights. Likely compliant.

14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP; 14.2 assigns Deliverables (subject to payment); 14.3/13.2 give a perpetual licence to embedded Vendor Technology; 14.4 handles joint IP and feedback. Check 15.1 no-training/no-sale restriction and definitional carve-outs in 1.3/1.4/1.8.

13.1 extends access to Affiliates, contractors and Authorized Users; 13.2 grants a perpetual paid-up licence; 13.3 limits revocation/suspension to material uncured breach after notice and cure. Confirm 13.4 restrictions are not overbroad.

Section 22.1 permits Vendor audits at any time without notice and with remote access to Customer systems — likely deviation on frequency, notice and on-site/system access, even though 22.2 (cost allocation, 5% threshold, no direct system access) and 22.3 (confidentiality of findings) are protective and conflict with 22.1.

Section 7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages on Customer for any dependency delay — liquidated damages against us, likely deviation. Note no reciprocal service credits appear in the outline.

19.1–19.3 give services, conformity, malicious-code and compliance warranties (90 days for Deliverables, term-long for hosted Services); 19.4 provides repair/re-perform with refund and termination fallback and preserves other remedies; 19.5 disclaimer is mutual and carved back. Likely compliant.

Section 18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O and USD 5M cyber cover for the term plus one year; 18.2 covers certificates, primacy, cancellation notice and non-limitation of liability. Likely compliant.

Section 2.1 expressly disclaims minimum quantity or purchase commitment and confirms non-ordering is not a breach; 7.1 bars minimum-use charges and 12.3 disclaims minimum-volume commitments. Likely compliant; no take-or-pay identified.

Section 11 provides up to six months' transition assistance at expiring rates, data return within thirty days in machine-readable form with no hostage-taking for fee disputes, and certified deletion; 10.1–10.2 cover surviving rights, delivery of Deliverables and refunds. Likely compliant.
